title: Spread Out the Stalls
statement:
A barn has stalls at the given `positions` along a line (all different, in any order). You must put `animals` animals in **different stalls** so that the **smallest distance between any two animals** is as **large** as possible.

Return that largest possible smallest distance.

examples.explanation: Use the stalls 1, 4 and 8 (or 1, 4 and 9): the closest pair is 3 apart. A distance of 4 is not possible: after 1 the next stall at least 4 away is 8, and then none is left.
All three stalls must be used: positions 1, 4, 7 are 3 apart.

expected.time: O(n log n + n log(max position))

hints.nudge: Suppose somebody claims 'the smallest distance can be d'. Can you check the claim quickly, by placing the animals greedily from the left?
hints.pattern: Binary search on the distance: a distance is possible if a greedy placement (always take the leftmost stall that is far enough from the last animal) fits all the animals; if d is possible, every smaller distance is possible too.
hints.pseudocode:
sort positions
fits(d): placed = 1; last = positions[0]; for p in the rest: if p - last >= d: placed += 1; last = p; return placed >= animals
lo = 1; hi = max - min
while lo < hi: mid = (lo + hi + 1) / 2; if fits(mid) lo = mid else hi = mid - 1
return lo
hints.walkthrough: Trying every way to choose the stalls is exponential. Turn the problem around: fix a distance d and ask whether the animals fit with every two at least d apart. Greedy works for that question: put the first animal in the leftmost stall, then always the next animal into the first stall that is at least d from the previous one (an earlier stall can never be worse, it leaves the most room). If you can place all the animals, d is possible. If d is possible then every smaller distance is possible too, so the possible distances form a prefix 1, 2, ..., D and you want its end D: binary search for the last distance that fits. Because you look for the LAST true value, round the middle UP ((lo + hi + 1) / 2) or the loop will not end. d = 1 always fits (the stalls are all different and there are enough of them).
